lessons.title: Load a glTF scene
lessons.concept: An asset can contain a hierarchy
body: glTF is a common format for delivering 3D scenes and models. A .glb packs glTF data into a binary file. Models may contain several meshes, materials, and animations rather than a single mesh.

GLTFLoader returns a result whose scene is the model’s root. This lesson parses a tiny embedded glTF so there are no downloads. In your own app, use await loader.loadAsync(url) and handle loading failures. Scale the loaded root just like any other object.
lessons.task: Set model.scale to 1.5 on every axis.
lessons.hint: Use model.scale.setScalar(1.5). The loaded root is a Group.

quiz.question: Where is a loaded glTF’s visible root?
quiz.explanation: GLTFLoader exposes the loaded scene hierarchy as gltf.scene.

lessons.title: Reach inside a model
body: Imported models are often groups nested inside other groups. Setting a material on the root group will not recolor its mesh children.

traverse visits an object and all of its descendants. Test isMesh before touching material properties. Real assets can use material arrays; this example has one material per mesh. Clone shared materials when you want to change one object without changing its siblings.
lessons.hint: The traversal applies this tint to each mesh in the loaded scene.

quiz.question: Why test isMesh while traversing?
options: A hierarchy can also contain groups, lights, and cameras
Every child is always a mesh
quiz.explanation: Different Object3D subclasses expose different properties.

lessons.title: Measure and center a model
body: A Box3 can measure an object’s world-space bounds, including its descendants. Its center is useful when an imported asset is offset from the origin.

Our object is deliberately displaced. Subtract its bounding-box center to bring it back to the origin. This example is a direct scene child; with transformed parents, convert the world-space center into the appropriate local space first.
lessons.task: Uncomment mesh.position.sub(center) to center the object.
lessons.hint: The bounds and center are already computed from the displaced mesh.

quiz.question: Box3.setFromObject measures…
quiz.explanation: It computes an axis-aligned bounding box around the object hierarchy.

lessons.title: Play a keyframe clip
body: A keyframe track stores property values at particular times. An AnimationClip groups tracks, and an AnimationMixer applies their interpolated values to an object as time advances.

Imported glTF assets can provide clips in gltf.animations. Here we build a tiny track ourselves: the cube moves up and comes down over two seconds. Starting the action and updating the mixer each frame are both required.
lessons.task: Uncomment action.play() to start the keyframe animation.
lessons.hint: The mixer already receives delta in onFrame.

quiz.question: What advances the animation mixer?
quiz.explanation: The mixer needs elapsed time to evaluate its active animation actions.

lessons.title: Leave no GPU memory behind
body: Removing an object from a scene stops it being drawn, but does not free its GPU geometry or material resources. Call dispose on resources when nothing else uses them. Shared geometry or materials must stay alive until their last user is done.

This workspace cleans up the current scene, controls, and renderer after each run. Your own app also needs to clean up event listeners and animation resources. Dispose this temporary geometry before it is forgotten; its dispose event gives us a visible check.
lessons.hint: The temporary geometry is not used by the displayed mesh, so it is safe to dispose.

quiz.question: Does scene.remove(mesh) dispose its geometry?
quiz.explanation: Scene membership and GPU resource lifetime are separate responsibilities.
